name: two-coordinate diagonal-conditioning baseline, quadratic map (axes design)

model.ansatz: square_lattice_ansatz(16): 16 one-body Z_i and 24 open 4x4 nearest-neighbour Z_iZ_j generators (40 phases)
model.input_state: fixed |0>^16 for every condition (standard IQP Born machine); AngleEncoder with zero RY angles
model.circuit: q(x|u,v) = |<x| H^16 exp(i sum_g theta_g(u,v) Z_g) H^16 |0>^16|^2
model.diagonal_map: theta(u,v) = w_0 + u w_u + v w_v + u^2 w_uu + v^2 w_vv
model.weights_layout: flattened (5,40) array with rows w_0, w_u, w_v, w_uu, w_vv
model.initialization: w_0 = init_scale * numpy default_rng(initialization stream).normal(0, 1, 40) plus one_body_mean on the 16 one-body entries; every other row zero. The initialization stream is shared with the input-conditioning fit of the same stage, repeat and start.
model.rationale: Pre-empts the objection that the affine map is too weak: adds the separable second-order terms u^2 and v^2, which axis-only training identifies. A u*v term is unidentifiable under axis training (zero on every fitting condition) and is excluded. The |+>^16 input is excluded because H D(theta) H |+> is proportional to |+> and gives the uniform law for every theta.

deviations: The fixed |0> input does not pin the origin: the model at (0,0) is theta = w_0 and is learned, not architecturally uniform. A one-body phase of pi/4 on every qubit (all other phases zero) gives the uniform distribution; the one-body mean range [0, pi/2] contains it.
limitations: Baseline for the axes design only.
Development selection uses exact target probabilities, as in the parent protocol.
Quadratic separable theta map fixed; no search over richer condition maps.
